message.content: {"quality": false, "reason": "The candidate proposes a 'Fallback to Visual Inspection' strategy that relies on the model's unaided visual perception ('direct visual inspection') when specialized tools fail. This is unsafe and unsupported because: 1) The source trajectory demonstrates that multiple expert tools (CheXagent, Maira2, LLaVA-Med) all returned negative results for surgical instruments, indicating the finding is likely below the detection threshold or absent; overriding this consensus with unverified visual inspection invites hallucination. 2) The candidate's reasoning claims to identify 'metallic density... in the lower abdominal region' corresponding to the 'right abdomen', but the provided lateral chest X-ray shows no obvious metallic foreign bodies in the abdomen (only faint spinal hardware/clip artifacts near the diaphragm/spine which are central/posterior, not clearly right-abdominal). 3) Relying on 'visual inspection' as a fallback bypasses the safety guardrails established by the tool suite. The correct behavior upon universal negative tool response should be to accept the negative finding or request higher-resolution imaging, not to substitute human-like (but model-unreliable) visual guessing.", "duplicate_of": null}
